posts.name: MigrantP

What you seem to be ignoring, and I keep trying to emphasize, is that the face down card is already in play. Therefore, if Fixed Point is in play, it is indestructible. When it's flipped face-up, it does not leave play in order to be treated as if it enters play. It's still in play, and by the definition of indestructible, it cannot leave play for any reason. But since it's limited, and another copy is in play, it is not permitted to stay in play. The only action that satisifies both of these existing rules is to flip the card back face down, keeping the card in play but making it no longer have a limited keyword. There is no "trumping" involved.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
I would set up discards like this: let the players drag the cards into the order they want (like we order the heroes in the set up screen), and then set a break point.  Then when they press "Go" discard all the cards up until the breakpoint, at which point they have the opportunity to discard more cards the same way, or to stop discarding.  You can put the breakpoint at the end of the line in order to discard all, but if the break point isn't set at all, a dialog box will pop up saying "Do you want to discard everything?" (Alternatively, you must set a breakpoint, but you can discard everything by setting the breakpoint at the end)

Actually, I would set up damage ordering the same way.  Drag the targets into the order you want, set a pause point (if you want), and then press Go.
